title: Eventual local finiteness on one affine target open after an affine stage
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preorder, $D:I^{\rm op}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $c$ a limit cone [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\le k$ and a morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ over $S_{i_0}=D(i_0)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $f_i$ and $f$ for its base changes to $S_i$ and the limit, and $p_{i0}:Y_i\to Y_0$, $p_0:Y\to Y_0$ for the first pullback projections. Suppose $f_k$ is affine. Let $V\subseteq Y_0$ be an affine open [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], and suppose the restriction $f|_{p_0^{-1}(V)}$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then there exist $j\ge k$ such that for every $i\ge j$, the restriction $f_i|_{p_{i0}^{-1}(V)}$ is finite. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assumption on $S_{i_0},X_0,Y_0$ is required.

proof.text: Put $V_k=p_{k0}^{-1}(V)$, where $p_{k0}:Y_k\to Y_0$ is the first pullback projection. It is affine because $p_{k0}$ is a base change of the affine transition $S_k\to S_0$. The preimage $U_k=f_k^{-1}(V_k)$ is affine by the assumed affineness of $f_k$. Cartesian-square pasting identifies, for every $i\ge k$ and for the limit, the restrictions over the preimage of $V$ with base changes of $U_k\to V_k$. The latter map is locally of finite type by base-change stability and restriction.

proof.text: For each point $v\in V$ choose an affine open $W_b\subset S_0$ around its image and an affine open $V_b\subset V\cap (Y_0\to S_0)^{-1}(W_b)$ containing $v$. The affine-open basis allows this choice, and $V$ is affine and hence quasi-compact, so finitely many $V_b$ cover $V$. Pull these opens back to $k$. The base opens $W_{b,k}$ are affine; open fibre-product pasting identifies $V_{b,k}$ with $V_b\times_{W_b}W_{b,k}$, hence it is affine. Its inverse image $U_{b,k}$ under $f_k$ is affine. Put $A_{b,k}=\Gamma(W_{b,k})$, $B_{b,k}=\Gamma(V_{b,k})$ and $C_{b,k}=\Gamma(U_{b,k})$. Their structure morphisms are Spec of the induced ring maps and $\varphi_{b,k}:B_{b,k}\to C_{b,k}$ is of finite type.

proof.text: For fixed $b$, use the directed upper tail $I_{\ge k}$. The opens $W_{b,i}=f_{ik}^{-1}(W_{b,k})$ are affine and form an inverse system with affine transitions. Affine-transition limits identify their limit with $W_{b,S}=p_k^{-1}(W_{b,k})$. Write $A_b=\mathop{\rm colim}_{i\ge k}\Gamma(W_{b,i})$. The Spec adjunction identifies $W_{b,S}$ with $\operatorname{Spec} A_b$, compatibly with all projections: Spec of the colimit is a limit, and the isomorphism is the unique limit isomorphism. Transfer from the chosen limit of the cited theorem to the given cone using uniqueness of limits.

proof.text: Open pullback pasting and the affine-spectrum fibre-product isomorphism identify the later pieces with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{b,i}\otimes_{A_{b,k}}B_{b,k})$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{b,i}\otimes_{A_{b,k}}C_{b,k})$, and similarly at the limit with $A_b$. The map is Spec of $\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi_{b,k}$: both descriptions have the same two pullback components, so they agree by the pullback universal property. Restrict the local finite-limit hypothesis to $V_{b,S}$. The resulting coordinate ring map is finite; conjugating by the ring isomorphisms preserves this, by transporting a finite set of module generators and its spanning equations.

proof.text: Apply the finite-ring-map colimit descent lemma to $\varphi_{b,k}$ to get $j_b\ge k$ where the tensor-product map is finite. This persists above $j_b$. Explicitly, if $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ generate $A_{b,j_b}\otimes C_{b,k}$ over $A_{b,j_b}\otimes B_{b,k}$, write each $1\otimes c$ as $\sum_l\varphi_{b,j_b}(\beta_l)x_l$. After applying the transition ring maps this identity holds at $i\ge j_b$. Multiplying it by $a\otimes1$ expresses each $a\otimes c$ in the span of the images of $x_l$ over $A_{b,i}\otimes B_{b,k}$. Pure tensors generate additively, hence those images span the entire target. Thus the corresponding restricted scheme morphism is finite at every $i\ge j_b$.

proof.text: Directedness gives an upper bound $j$ of the finite set of $j_b$ together with $k$. For every $i\ge j$ the inverse images of $V_b$ cover the inverse image of $V$ in $Y_i$ and every restriction is finite by the preceding calculation. Finiteness local on the target yields finiteness of the restriction over the inverse image of $V$. If $V$ is empty, take $j=k$; finiteness follows from the empty open cover. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $S_0,X_0,Y_0$ is used: only the affine open $V$ must be quasi-compact.

mathlib_searches.query: Finiteness of a scheme morphism restricted to one affine target open eventually holds at stages of an inverse limit with affine transitions
Once a stage morphism is affine, finite type ring maps on one affine target open become finite at sufficiently large stages when finite over the inverse limit

theorem exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_baseChange_affine_open
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ k : I) (hk : i₀ ≤ k)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj (op i₀))) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left]
    (haffine : IsAffineHom (((Over.pullback (D.map (homOfLE hk).op)).map f₀).left))
    (V : Y₀.left.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hfinite : IsFinite
      ((((Over.pullback (c.π.app (op i₀))).map f₀).left) ∣_
        ((pullback.fst Y₀.hom (c.π.app (op i₀))) ⁻¹ᵁ V))) :
    ∃ (j : I) (hkj : k ≤ j), ∀ (i : I) (hji : j ≤ i),
      IsFinite
        ((((Over.pullback (D.map (homOfLE (hk.trans (hkj.trans hji))).op)).map f₀).left)
          ∣_ ((pullback.fst Y₀.hom
            (D.map (homOfLE (hk.trans (hkj.trans hji))).op)) ⁻¹ᵁ V))
